transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Lee. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Lee. Thank you so much for seeing me, I really appreciate you fitting me in. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time, it's probably just a little quirk I need to work through, but... well, I've been having a bit of trouble at work lately. 

I'm a jeweler, and, um... well, when customers ask me a really simple question—like, say, just asking when a ring repair is going to be ready—I try to give them a helpful answer, but my words just sort of... get away from me? I'll start talking about the repair invoices, which is normal, but then suddenly I'm bringing up garden soil, and then somehow I'm rambling about mortgage papers... and I can just see it in their eyes that I'm completely losing them. 

It's really quite embarrassing, honestly, because I want to be professional. I just want to be able to communicate clearly again. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it the right way for you.
Over the past few weeks, have you noticed any significant changes in your mood—like feeling unusually sad, hopeless, or on the other hand, unusually energetic, elated, or irritable?

Well, um... I guess I have been feeling a little bit down lately. Nothing too terrible, I promise, I'm sure everyone gets into a funk sometimes, right? But... I suppose most mornings, I wake up with this sort of... flat, heavy sadness. It's almost like all the color has just drained out of the house before I even get my coat on to head to the shop. 

I've been trying my best to push through it and keep a smile on for the customers, because I know it's not their fault I'm feeling this way. I really hope I'm not making a bigger deal out of this than it is. Does that sound like the kind of thing you were asking about? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Did the trouble with your words getting away from you start around the same time as this low, heavy mood, or did the speech problem begin separately, before or after the mood changes?

Oh, um... let me think about that. I want to make sure I'm giving you the timeline exactly right, so I don't confuse things. 

Actually, the... the thing with my words, and some other little odd things, started before I felt quite so sad. There was a stretch of time—maybe a few weeks?—where I wasn't feeling down at all. I was still running my jewelry-making classes and keeping up with my gardening just fine. But during that time, I... well, it's a little silly, but I kept hearing these noises coming from the polishing room when no one was in there. And I started getting this funny feeling that customers were... I don't know, watching the business? Like, keeping tabs on me? 

I know it sounds a bit strange when I say it out loud. I hope you don't think I'm completely losing my marbles! I just assumed I was working too hard and letting my imagination get the better of me. But yes, that all started for several weeks before the heavy sadness really settled in. Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of detail you were looking for.
Are you still hearing those noises or feeling like you're being watched right now, even on days when your mood feels a bit better?

Um, well... yes, a little bit, I suppose. I mean, I really don't want to make it sound like I'm completely falling apart or anything! But... yes, even on the days where the sadness isn't quite so heavy, I still catch myself looking over my shoulder, thinking someone is keeping tabs on us. 

But I should probably mention—just to make sure I'm giving you the whole picture, because I want to be helpful—that during the worst of it, like a few months ago when I was feeling just terribly down and couldn't even bring myself to care about my jewelry designs... those other things were happening at the exact same time. I'd be sitting there, feeling just awful and empty, and I'd hear someone calling my name from the empty shop floor. And I was just so convinced that the customers were secretly checking up on our payment records. 

I know that sounds so silly now, and I'm really trying to keep it all together. I hope I'm not overwhelming you with all this... is this the kind of information you need to figure out what's wrong with me?
Thinking back to when you first started hearing those noises and feeling watched, about how many months ago did all of this begin in total?

Oh, goodness... let me think back. I want to be as accurate as possible for you. Um... I suppose, if I really trace it back to the very beginning—the noises, and occasionally thinking I smelled something strange like burning metal when the torches were off, and worrying about the customers... it's been a little while. 

I'd say it started maybe... a year and eight months ago? Give or take? I really hope I'm remembering that right. I just kept trying to brush it off, you know, telling myself I just needed a vacation or more sleep. I feel terrible that I let it go on for so long before talking to someone. Does that timeline help you? I hope I haven't made things too complicated by waiting so long to mention it.

Over that entire year-and-eight-month period, if you add it all up, would you say the low, heavy sadness has been present for most of that time, or has it only shown up during shorter stretches while the noises and feelings of being watched continued on their own the rest of the time?

Oh, um... well, I don't want to sound like a complainer, because I know everyone has their bad days, but... yes, if I really add it all up, that low, heavy sadness has been there for most of that time. 

It hasn't just been a bad week here or there. For the majority of that year and eight months, it's just been this... this bleak feeling that I can't shake. Along with the trouble sleeping, and not really having much of an appetite, and just feeling so guilty about... well, everything, really. It's been pretty much a daily struggle for most of this whole ordeal. 

I try my best to put on a brave face for the classes, of course! I don't want to bring anyone else down. But... yes, the sadness has been there most of the time, alongside the other things. I hope I'm explaining that clearly enough? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so you can help me sort this out.

Oh, gosh, I'm so sorry... I don't think I quite caught what you just said. My mind just went blank for a second. I really want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need to figure this all out—could you possibly repeat that for me? I hope I'm not being too much of a bother or slowing things down!

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a chronic (~20 month) illness featuring persistent psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations of voices/noises, olfactory hallucinations, and paranoid delusions of being watched/monitored) alongside disorganized speech (tangentiality). Critically, there was a period of several weeks where psychotic symptoms occurred in the absence of any mood disturbance, satisfying the criterion for psychotic symptoms outside a mood episode. Subsequently, a major depressive episode developed (depressed mood, anhedonia, sleep/appetite disturbance, guilt) that has co-occurred with the psychotic symptoms for the majority of the illness duration. This combination—psychosis without mood symptoms for a distinct period, plus a mood episode present for the majority of the total illness duration—meets criteria for schizoaffective disorder, depressive type, rather than major depressive disorder with psychotic features (where psychosis is confined to mood episodes) or schizophrenia (which would require the mood episode to be brief relative to the psychotic illness).
